chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Muskan, from Muyassar, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

He said to me: 'Do you isolate yourselves, converse, and say whatever you wish?' So I said, 'Yes, by Allah, we do isolate ourselves, converse, and say whatever we wish.' He said: 'By Allah, I would love to be with you in some of those places. By Allah, I love your scent and your spirits, and indeed you are upon the Religion of Allah and the Religion of His Angels, so assist with piety and striving.'

key_terms.اجْتِهَادٍ: striving or exertion in religious practice
key_terms.تَخْلُونَ: to isolate oneself or seclude oneself

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) say about the companions who isolated themselves for conversation?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the concept of *al-khalwah* (seclusion) among the faithful as a space for authentic spiritual discourse, where Imam al-Baqir expresses a deep affection for their 'breath and souls,' signifying their inner purity. He validates their adherence to the Religion of Allah and His Angels, urging them to preserve this status through *war'* (ascetic piety) and *ijtihad* (scholarly striving), emphasizing that true faith is maintained through both inner devotion and outward effort. This reflects the Shia emphasis on the community of the righteous as a spiritual entity distinct from the general populace.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Muskan, from Muyassar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

having said to me: ‘Are you isolating yourselves, and discussing and saying whatever you so desire to?’ So I said, ‘Yes, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! We do isolate ourselves, and we discuss, and we are saying whatever we so desire to’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! I<sup>asws</sup> would love to be with you in one of those places. But, by Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, I<sup>asws</sup> loved your aromas, and your spirits, and you all are upon the Religion of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and the Religion of His<sup>azwj</sup> Angels, therefore Assist with piety and the striving’.
en.sarwar: 5. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Faddal from ibn Muskan from Muyassir who has said the following:

“Once abu Ja’far (a.s.) asked me, ‘Do you hold private gatherings wherein you say whatever you want?’ I said, ‘Yes, I swear by Allah, we hold private gatherings and say whatever we like to say (in praise of Muhammad and his family).’ The Imam said, ‘I swear by Allah, I wish I could be with you at such gatherings. I swear by Allah, I love your fragrance and your spirits. You, certainly, follow the religion of Allah, and the religion of the angels. Pay attention to restraining from the worldly attractions (sins) and assist yourselves with striving hard in work.’”
